n192f21c0e79.s: Groups such as Keralites and Sikhs are cited as examples of which factor that influences migration?
n192f21c0e79.x: Information networks associated with groups such as Keralites and Sikhs influence migration decisions.

n538e991ef7d.s: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC), giving NFSA ration portability, is operational in how many States/UTs?

ne7e8683f145.s: Which of the following pairs about the World Migration Report is correctly matched?
ne7e8683f145.x: The IOM publishes the World Migration Report, brought out biennially since 2000; the 2026 report is the 13th edition.

n006bc871817.s: Migration decided by weighing push and pull factors is classified as:
n006bc871817.x: Weighing push and pull factors marks voluntary migration; persecution, displacement and exploitation cause forced migration.

na443ab83110.s: Which Labour Code covers workers who migrate on their own and provides them an annual travel allowance?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
na443ab83110.x: The OSH Code, 2020 covers self-migrating workers, provides an annual travel allowance and supports PDS and social security portability.

nb178798559e.s: The four Labour Codes, which came into force in November 2025, consolidated how many laws?
nb178798559e.x: The four Labour Codes consolidated 29 laws and came into force in November 2025.

n02a77ed4925.s: Which 2011 urban agglomeration, with about 8.7 million people, was NOT large enough to be a mega city?
n02a77ed4925.x: Only Greater Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata had 10 million or more in 2011; Chennai had about 8.7 million.

n795054555d8.s: The 1981 Census town criteria have been criticised for having a:
n795054555d8.x: The criticisms are male bias, uniform thresholds and density measured on administrative boundaries, not satellite imagery.

nf459c214beb.s: Which of the following is identified as a cause of urbanisation in India?
o: Falling pressure of population on rural land
nf459c214beb.x: Growth of industry and trade, pressure of population on rural land, low farm productivity, services and transport are causes of urbanisation.

n0572058bd65.s: Which of the following pairs about Census 2011 is correctly matched?
n0572058bd65.x: Census 2011 counted about 6.54 crore people living in slums.

n20ea582f397.s: Which of the following town – period of origin pairs is correctly matched?
n20ea582f397.x: Bhubaneswar, like Chandigarh, Gandhinagar and Dispur, is a post-1947 planned town; Hyderabad and Jaipur are medieval, Pataliputra ancient.

n483d578e8ed.s: Which of the following State – National Capital Region status pairs is correctly matched?
n483d578e8ed.x: The NCR comprises NCT of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan; Punjab is not part of it.

nc1c9508a66a.s: Rohtak and Karnal are towns of the National Capital Region in which State?
nc1c9508a66a.x: Rohtak and Karnal are in the Haryana part of the NCR; Khurja (Bulandshahr) is in the UP part, and Ambala is not in the NCR.

new.s: In the Census, a 'lifetime migrant' is identified on the basis of:
new.x: Lifetime migration is counted by place of birth; the Census also counts migrants by place of last residence.

new.s: Temporary, seasonal, permanent and return migration are types classified on the basis of:
new.x: Time is the basis for temporary/seasonal, permanent and return migration; boundary gives internal/international.

new.s: Which migration stream is the smallest and is linked with counter-urbanisation?
new.x: Urban-to-rural is the smallest stream, made up of return migration and counter-urbanisation.

new.s: Which one of the following statements about migration streams in India is NOT correct?
o: Rural-to-rural was the largest stream in 2011
Rural-to-urban migration is dominated by males seeking employment
Rural-to-rural migration is mainly female, due to marriage
new.x: Rural-to-rural, not rural-to-urban, is the largest stream (UPPSC 2017 trap).

new.s: According to PLFS 2020-21, what share of female migrants moved for marriage?
new.x: 86.8% of female migrants moved for marriage; 47.9% is the female migration rate.

new.s: According to PLFS 2020-21, the main reason for male migration, accounting for 22.8% of male migrants, was:
new.x: Men migrate mainly for employment (22.8%); women mainly for marriage.

new.s: Political instability in the area of origin is an example of a:
new.x: Conflict and political instability at the origin push people out; jobs, wages and amenities pull them to destinations.

new.s: The 'Laws of Migration' (1885) were given by:
new.x: E.G. Ravenstein gave the laws of migration in 1885; Lee gave the push-pull theory in 1966.

new.s: The demographic transition theory is associated with:
new.x: Demographic transition is linked with Notestein and Thompson, not Lee; Doubleday gave the diet theory.

new.s: According to Census 2011, which States lead as sources of out-migration?
new.x: UP and Bihar lead as source States; Delhi and Maharashtra lead as destinations.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011 migration data:
1. Migrants by last residence numbered about 455.8 million.
2. Over 4.1 crore people were inter-State migrants.
3. Delhi and Maharashtra were the leading States of out-migration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Census 2011 counted 455.8 million migrants and over 4.1 crore inter-State migrants; Delhi and Maharashtra are leading destinations, not sources.

new.s: Which continent has the highest percentage share of international migrants in its population?
new.x: Oceania has the highest percentage of migrants; Europe has the largest number.

new.s: Which region hosts the largest number of international migrants?
new.x: Europe hosts the most migrants by number, while Oceania leads by percentage.

new.s: The International Organization for Migration (IOM), publisher of the World Migration Report, was set up in:
new.x: The IOM was set up in 1951; its World Migration Report has been biennial since 2000.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration?
o: It was adopted at Marrakech in December 2018
It was endorsed by all UN member countries
new.x: The GCM was not endorsed by all countries; it is non-binding, covers only international migration and was adopted at Marrakech in December 2018.

new.s: India has the world's largest diaspora, numbering about:
new.x: India's diaspora is the largest at over 35 million; about 3.5 million live in the UAE.

new.s: Under the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979, the displacement allowance was ____ of monthly wages.
new.x: The Act gave a displacement allowance of 50% of monthly wages plus a journey allowance.

new.s: The e-Shram portal, a One-Stop-Solution for unorganised workers, was launched in:
new.x: e-Shram was launched in 2021; it links 15 schemes and is available in 22 languages.

new.s: The Telugu diaspora is concentrated mainly in:
new.x: Telugu migrants go mainly to the Gulf countries and the USA.

new.s: Which Andhra Pradesh body runs a help desk for Gulf migrants?
new.x: APNRT runs the Gulf help desk for migrants from Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: A place without urban status that meets the Census urban criteria is called a:
new.x: A census town has no municipal status but meets the Census criteria; a statutory town is notified with a ULB.

new.s: The Census town criteria, retained for Census 2027, were set in:
new.x: The criteria were set in 1981 and the RGI keeps them for Census 2027.

new.s: The slow phase of urbanisation in India covers the period:
new.x: The slow phase was 1901–31, the medium 1931–61 and the rapid from 1961.

new.s: India's urban share in Census 2001 was:
new.x: The urban share was 27.81% in 2001 and 31.16% in 2011.

new.s: According to the World Bank (2010), what share of Indians lived in 'urban-like' areas?
new.x: The World Bank put 55.3% in urban-like areas; the EAC-PM estimated about 63% for 2015.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's urbanisation during 2001–11:
1. Statutory towns rose from 3,799 to 4,041.
2. The rural share in 2011 was 68.84%.
3. Decadal urban growth was 41.8%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statutory towns rose to 4,041 and rural share was 68.84%; decadal urban growth was 31.8%, not 41.8%.

new.s: In the Census class-size classification, a Class VI town has a population of:
new.x: Class VI towns have below 5,000 people; Class I towns have 1,00,000 and above.

new.s: In the Census class-size classification, a Class III town has a population of:
new.x: Class III is 20,000–49,999; Class II is 50,000–99,999 and Class IV 10,000–19,999.

new.s: Which State had the largest urban population in Census 2011?
new.x: Maharashtra had the largest urban population (50.8 million); Goa had the highest urban share.

new.s: Which State had the largest number of census towns in 2011?
new.x: West Bengal led in census towns, mostly around Kolkata, followed by Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

new.s: Which was the least urbanised State in Census 2011?
new.x: Himachal Pradesh (10.04%) was the least urbanised, followed by Bihar and Assam.

new.s: Which State/UT had the highest urban share overall in Census 2011?
new.x: NCT Delhi (97.50%) had the highest urban share; Goa (62.17%) was the most urbanised State.

new.s: In the functional classification of towns, Ankleshwar is a:
new.x: Ankleshwar is a mining town (APPSC G2 2025); Jamshedpur is the industrial example.

new.s: Udhampur is an example of which functional type of town?
new.x: Udhampur, like Secunderabad, Ambala and Mhow, is a garrison/cantonment town.

new.s: Which of the following town – function pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Pilani is an educational town; Araku is a resort, Bhadrachalam a religious and Digboi a mining town.

new.s: The Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA) was set up in:
new.x: KMDA was set up in 1970, after DDA (1957); CMDA followed in 1974 and MMRDA in 1975.

new.s: Which of the following cities is NOT a planned city?
new.x: Bengaluru is not a planned city; Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar and Navi Mumbai are.

new.s: How many functions are listed in the Twelfth Schedule added by the 74th Amendment?
new.x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions, such as urban planning and slum improvement.

new.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on:
new.x: The 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993.

new.s: After 15 cities were merged, AMRUT now covers how many cities?
new.x: AMRUT began with 500 cities; it now covers 485 after 15 were merged.

new.s: PMAY-Urban 2.0 aims to provide housing to how many families by 2028-29?
new.x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore families with ₹2.30 lakh crore by 2028-29.

new.s: The SPM Rurban Mission (2016), focused on rural clusters with urban traits, is run by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
new.x: The Rurban Mission is under the Ministry of Rural Development and targets rural clusters, not cities.

new.s: The concept of the 'Right to the City' was given by:
new.x: Henri Lefebvre set out the Right to the City in Le Droit à la Ville (1968).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about APMCHUD:
1. It was set up in 2006.
2. Its permanent secretariat is hosted by India.
3. Its 6th edition was held in Baku in 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: APMCHUD was set up in 2006 with its secretariat hosted by India; the 6th edition was in New Delhi in 2016.

new.s: The first meeting of APMCHUD was held in:
new.x: APMCHUD's first meeting was held in New Delhi.

new.s: UN-Habitat signed an MoU with Andhra Pradesh in July 2026 for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:
new.x: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is to be at Amaravati.

new.s: According to UN-Habitat's World Cities Report 2026, how many people live in slums worldwide?
new.x: The report puts 1.1 billion people in slums; 3.4 billion face housing shortage.

new.s: The term 'conurbation' was coined by:
new.x: Patrick Geddes coined conurbation; Gottmann used megalopolis.

new.s: The concept of the 'primate city' is associated with:
new.x: Mark Jefferson defined a primate city as several times larger than the next city.

new.s: The German term 'Umland' refers to:
o: A chain of merged metropolitan areas
The area surrounding a town and linked to it
A city several times larger than the next
A city of 10 million or more
new.x: Umland is the area surrounding a town and linked to it, its hinterland (UPPSC 2017).

new.s: In the UN DESA World Urbanization Prospects 2025, New Delhi is ranked:
new.x: WUP 2025 ranks Jakarta 1st, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi 4th.

new.s: India's urban population is projected to reach about ____ by 2050.
new.x: India's urban population is projected at 951 million by 2050.

new.s: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) was set up in:
new.x: MMRDA was set up in 1975, after DDA (1957), KMDA (1970) and CMDA (1974).

new.s: Which authority plans the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region?
new.x: VMRDA plans Visakhapatnam; APCRDA runs Amaravati.

new.s: Which Rajasthan town is part of the National Capital Region?
new.x: Alwar is the Rajasthan town in the NCR.

new.s: Which Article provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee for every metropolitan area?
new.x: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees; Article 243P defines a metropolitan area.

new.s: The 74th Amendment, 1992 inserted which Part into the Constitution?
new.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA on municipalities.

new.s: Under Article 243P, a metropolitan area has a population of:
new.x: Article 243P defines a metropolitan area as having 10 lakh or more people.

new.s: Which State had the largest number of slum dwellers in Census 2011?
new.x: Maharashtra had the largest slum number; undivided AP had the highest slum share (~36%).

new.s: Which city had the largest number of slum dwellers in Census 2011?
new.x: Greater Mumbai had the largest number; Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest share (~44%).

new.s: Using a broader definition, the World Bank estimates India's slum dwellers at about:
new.x: The World Bank puts slum dwellers at 177 million, against the Census figure of 6.54 crore.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about municipal solid waste in India:
1. About 62 million tonnes are generated a year.
2. About 70% of it is processed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India generates about 62 million tonnes a year; about 70% is collected but only 30% processed.

new.s: Swachh Survekshan, for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, is conducted by the:
new.x: The Quality Council of India conducts Swachh Survekshan for MoHUA.

new.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, Indore led the Super Swachh League for the:
new.x: Indore has been the cleanest city eight times.

new.s: Which city topped the new Swachh Shahar category (10 lakh+) in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
new.x: Ahmedabad topped the new Swachh Shahar 10 lakh+ category, ahead of Bhopal and Lucknow.

new.s: How many cities were covered by Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
new.x: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016 with 73 cities and covered 4,589 in 2024-25.
